sentiment.rationale: The document shows strong operational momentum with record quarterly revenues across all five businesses and positive operating leverage for the firm and each business. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to 'exceed $84 billion' from a prior expectation of 'at least $84 billion', and NII ex-Markets guidance was raised to 'up around 5.5%' from a prior expectation. However, expenses were guided higher than previously expected, and the CET1 ratio declined to 13.2% from 13.5% QoQ due to buybacks and RWA growth, partially offsetting the positive revenue momentum. The score reflects a genuine guidance raise on the top line, tempered by expense growth and capital consumption.

summary.revenue: Total revenues of $22.1 billion in 3Q25, up 9% YoY. Year-to-date revenues of $65.4 billion, up 7% YoY.
summary.eps: Diluted EPS of $1.86 in 3Q25, up 23% YoY from $1.51. Excluding the notable item (goodwill impairment), EPS was $2.24.
summary.guidance: Full-year 2025 revenues expected to exceed $84 billion. NII ex-Markets expected to be up around 5.5% for the full year. Full-year expenses expected to be higher than previously guided ($53.4 billion), with the efficiency ratio slightly below 64% excluding the goodwill impairment. Targeting 10-11% RoTCE in 2026.
summary.margin: Efficiency ratio of 64.7% in 3Q25, improved 30 bps YoY. Excluding the notable item, the efficiency ratio was 61.4%, improved ~360 bps YoY. Net interest margin (NIM) was 2.40% in 3Q25, down 11 bps QoQ and up 7 bps YoY.
key_risks: Goodwill impairment of $726 million related to the Banamex transaction, recorded in Other expenses.
Corporate non-accrual loans increased 119% YoY to $2.1 billion, driven by idiosyncratic downgrades in Markets and Banking.
Consumer non-accrual loans increased 32% YoY to $1.6 billion, primarily driven by Wealth due to California wildfires.
CET1 Capital ratio declined to 13.2% from 13.5% QoQ, driven by common share repurchases, higher RWA, and dividends.
Expenses guided higher than previously expected for the full year.
Markets revenues expected to see a sequential decline from 3Q to 4Q that could exceed the historical range of 15-20%.
Uncertainty around the Federal Reserve's SCB averaging rule, leading to a higher CET1 target of 12.8%.
key_opportunities: Record quarterly revenues in all five businesses (Services, Markets, Banking, Wealth, USPB).
Services posted its best quarter ever with revenues up 7%.
Markets delivered its best third quarter ever with revenues up 15%.
Wealth had record Net New Investment Assets of $18.6 billion.
USPB had a record quarter with revenues up 7% and 12 consecutive quarters of positive operating leverage.
Investment Banking fees up 17% YoY with continued market share gains.
Returned over $6 billion to common shareholders in 3Q25, including $5 billion in share repurchases.
Announced agreement to sell a 25% equity stake in Banamex, a significant step toward divestiture.
Continued progress on transformation with over two-thirds of programs at or near target state.
Investments in AI and digital assets driving innovation and improved capabilities.
